speaker: Doctor
text: I will ask you a few questions to better understand your symptoms. First, can you describe exactly where your neck pain is located and how it radiates to your arms?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of diabetes and the progressive nature of your symptoms, I need to determine if this is related to a cervical spine issue or diabetic neuropathy. Has your pain or weakness ever improved with rest or changing positions? Also, have you noticed any numbness in your legs or feet?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical Spine

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your MRI of the cervical spine is normal, this makes a structural cause like a herniated disc unlikely. Given your history of diabetes and the burning nature of your pain, could you tell me if you experience any "pins and needles" in your feet or legs as well? Also, have you noticed any muscle wasting or weakness in your upper arms or shoulders?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS). The combination of progressive upper and lower motor neuron signs (weakness, fasciculations, absent reflexes) alongside sensory complaints, in the absence of structural cervical pathology, is highly indicative of ALS.
